answer: The area of water is 0.3052 km², as calculated from the SAR backscatter analysis using a threshold of -16.0 dB. This water mask, derived from VV polarization, covers 3052 pixels, which corresponds to the northern-western quadrant of the image. The optical water mask (from tools.water_highlight) identifies a much larger area (14,705 pixels), but the two masks disagree significantly, with an IoU of only 0.020048. The SAR-based water detection is more consistent with the pixel-scale resolution (10.0 m) and the calibrated backscatter statistics. The water is concentrated in the NW quadrant, which also has the highest pixel count for water (849 pixels) among the four quadrants.
